prompt: A real night photograph on 35 mm colour-negative film, vertical 9:16, taken from a seat in the middle of a rain-soaked roadside shelter on an ordinary London street, the lens pulled a little wider so more of the road shows. Across the top, the shelter's roof frame and wet glass canopy dripping water; down the left edge, the glass side wall streaked with rain and faintly mirroring the inside; slightly left of centre, the shelter's lit end advertising case, turned a little toward us, displaying the poster from the reference image, reproduced exactly, the same man's face. The open front on the right shows a broad stretch of wet two-lane road running sideways across the frame and curving away into the distance on the right, traffic keeping to the left as in Britain. Coming up the lane nearest the shelter's kerb, travelling toward the camera with the kerb on its left, a British ambulance, tall box van body with yellow-green chequered Battenburg panels, headlights blazing and blue lights flashing, about half a street away and closing, big enough to read as an ambulance but still well short of the shelter. Its blue light washes across the wet tarmac in long streaks and throws a soft blue sheen onto the edge of the shelter glass on the right. In the far lane two cars head the other way with red tail lights glowing in the spray. Light sources: a row of sodium-orange street lamps, the poster's white backlight, the ambulance's blue lights and headlights, red tail lights in the far lane, dim curtained windows of the houses opposite. Wet tarmac, sodium orange against cold teal shadow, heavy film grain, halation, rain falling through every beam. No readable text except the poster; no number plates, no signs, no lettering on the ambulance. Photo-real, not CGI. Thanks.
